A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AFL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original AFL evaluations on standard and electric VRPs, comparisons with other solvers, agent ablations and additional routing benchmarks.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds runtime analysis, alternative-LLM and input-format evaluations, and large-instance results.

M1.justification: The three-subtask, four-agent pipeline, destroy-insert heuristic, simulated annealing and Appendix D prompts are retained. v2 adds implementation explanations for small-instance code reuse and a 10-second timeout; v1 Appendix D.3.1 already illustrates timeout-driven debugging, so these disclosures do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: v2 adds JSON and CSV input conditions and CVRPLib-XXL instances spanning approximately 3,000–16,000 customers, versus the earlier CVRPLib evaluation up to 1,000 customers. These substantially extend input conditions and the evaluated scale regime. Renamed variants in the constraint table retain their original constraints.

E2.justification: POMO and LEHD become evaluated comparators in the new CVRPLib-XXL comparison, Table 18. POMO is distinct from the previously evaluated RF-POMO. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark and prompting comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Added studies evaluate Claude-Sonnet-4-20250514 and GPT-4o alongside GPT-4.1, introduce intermediate improvement budgets in Figure 4, and distinguish single-instance solver-generation timing from testing over 1,000 instances. The XXL experiment also documents generation from a small exemplar followed by large-instance execution. These extend evaluation design without establishing reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained JA/RA ablations, v2 adds backbone sensitivity, robustness to JSON/CSV representations, phase-specific runtime analysis and a more detailed quality-versus-iterations/time study (C.4, C.10–C.11 and Figure 4). These address several previously untested dependencies and practical trade-offs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables and curves continue the existing reporting practice without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 10 and 16–18 and Figure 4 add runtime, backbone, input-format and large-instance results. For example, Table 18 reports AFL's 16.56% gap against LEHD's 40.76% on B2(16k). Matched original benchmark results remain unchanged; the additions are new evaluations, not demonstrated before-and-after performance gains.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, destroy-strategy formalization, simulated-annealing equations and RER/SR definitions are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: automated, self-contained VRP solving through three subtasks and four agents, competitive performance across 60 VRP variants, and high code reliability and solution feasibility.

C2.justification: v2 interprets backbone strength as affecting heuristic quality while attributing stable reliability to agent coordination. It also discusses generation efficiency and quality–runtime trade-offs. The existing limitation concerning performance relative to specialized state-of-the-art solvers remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code/data repository pointer, OpenAI API and AMD EPYC 7702P/64 GB RAM details, generation timings, small-exemplar guidance and the 10-second timeout threshold. The explicit 16-CPU-core allocation in v1 is omitted. These improve technical disclosure without proving an underlying implementation or hardware change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ma et al. (2026), Jiang et al. (2025a), Zhang and Cao (2025), and Zhu et al. (2026), with brief contextual additions in the introduction and Appendix A. The main positioning against template-based, external-solver and direct-generation approaches is retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized explanations, four additional Appendix C subsections, terminology corrections, funding acknowledgments and conference headers. The appendix description is corrected from 'additional 32' to 'all 48' variants without changing that table's results. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with runtime, backbone, input-format and XXL tables (10 and 16–18), plus the two-panel Figure 4. The prompting comparison moves from main-text Table 7 to appendix Table 9. Original Figures 1–3 and most existing table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves code-generation cost unquantified and evaluates only GPT-4.1 with VRPLIB inputs. v2's cost breakdowns and backbone/input robustness tests make practicality and generality easier to assess, while its code/data pointer improves reproducibility information. These are useful gains, but sparse comparator settings for the new XXL evaluation and absent uncertainty reporting limit the strength of the additional evidence.
